what: The Bionic Reading Converter makes the first part of every word bold. Your eyes jump from one bold start to the next and your brain fills in the rest of each word.
You choose how much of each word is bold, whether the rest fades, and whether short words and numbers are included. The result copies as formatted text into email, Google Docs or Word, or as HTML.
uses: Make long articles and reports easier to skim.
Some people with ADHD or dyslexia find bolded word starts help them keep their place.
Convert notes or summaries before revising.
Paste formatted text into an email or document to try the style on readers.
tutorial: Type or paste any text. Paragraphs and line breaks are kept.
Move Bold part of each word between 10% and 90%. Around 40 to 50% suits most readers.
Optionally leave words shorter than 2, 3 or 4 letters unbolded.
Tick Fade the rest of each word for more contrast and change the preview size.
Copy formatted text pastes with bold into email, Docs and Word; Copy HTML code gives you the markup.
Download .html saves a simple page you can open on any device.
features: From 10% to 90% of each word, rounded to whole letters.
Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Indic scripts and Thai, with accents and combined letters kept whole.
Puts both formatted and plain text on the clipboard.
Each part of a word like well-known gets its own bold start.
Your text never leaves your browser.

example.title: An article for focused reading
example.text: Paste: Reading faster is fun. With 45% bold, Reading shows its first three letters in bold, faster shows fas in bold, and is and fun get their first letter in bold. Press Copy formatted text and paste into Google Docs to keep the bold parts.

tips: Try 40% first, then adjust to what feels comfortable.
Skip words shorter than 3 letters for a calmer look.
Use a larger preview size for long reading sessions.
If a website strips formatting, paste the HTML code instead.
problems: The bold parts disappear when pasting
The app only accepts plain text. Paste into an app that supports formatting, or use Copy HTML code.
Chinese or Japanese text is unchanged
These scripts do not have letters inside words to bold, so they are left as they are.
Some browsers block the clipboard. The text is then selected for you; press Ctrl+C or Cmd+C.
